pages.title: Harbour Light
pages.description: A year photographing a working harbour at dusk, for a book by The Quiet Press.

blocks.heading: The brief
blocks.body:
A small publisher asked for one picture of the harbour at the hour when the lights come on. I went back every week for a year.

The book, with its warm-grey paper and a single red thread in the binding, was designed alongside the photographs so each spread could breathe.

pages.title: Small Hours
pages.description: A night-time series about the windows that stay lit, shown at the Orrin Museum of Objects.

blocks.heading: The brief
blocks.body:
A museum wanted a quiet exhibition about the city after midnight.

I photographed one apartment block from the same spot for ninety nights and let the lit windows tell the story: shift workers, new parents, a student with a lamp.

pages.title: About
pages.description: About Juno Fairweather, a fictional photographer and art director.

members.name: Juno Fairweather
members.bio:
I make pictures for books, studios and small institutions. I trained in graphic design, fell for photography on a long ferry ride, and have been trying to do both well ever since.

I work alone, on a few projects a season, so each one gets the time it needs.
